victim: The finalist badge delivery and the registration desk
motive: To avoid a visible disruption before the evening sponsor photo, she asked for the replacement to be treated as the original batch.
method: She held B-17 in the logistics cage under her custody, requested the B-17R reprint on an approval reference that belonged to another order, and later said the original went to Kabir at 14:46.
explanation: The official custody trail breaks while Nisha is the recorded custodian. The records prove deliberate diversion and a cover-up, not what happened to the physical badges afterwards.

timeline.event: Aarav prints the original B-17 batch: 12 badges for registration
Nisha places B-17 on a quality hold with no failed measurement
B-17 enters the logistics cage under Nisha’s custody
A planned-route manifest is generated; it is not a handoff
Kabir scans an empty route tote
Nisha requests B-17R using approval reference APR-044
Registration receives an empty B-17 sleeve
Nisha says the original went to Kabir at 14:46

causal_chain: The original B-17 was in Nisha’s custody after 14:44.
No scan shows Kabir ever accepted it; his scan is an empty tote.
Nisha ordered a reprint on an approval reference that belongs to another order.
Her later statement conflicts with the custody trail and her messages show why.

resolution.motive: She wanted no visible delay before the sponsor photo and asked for the replacement to be treated as the original.
resolution.method: She held the original in her custody, ordered an unapproved reprint and misstated who had the original.
chain: The original B-17 was scanned into the cage under Nisha’s custody at 14:44.
Kabir’s only B-17 scan is an empty tote; the manifest is only a plan.
